title: Mexico’s Cry of Independence 2026: Thousands Arrive at Mexico City’s Zócalo
author: Emir Olivares Alonso and Kevin Ruiz
content:
_This article by[Emir Olivares
Alonso](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Emir%20Olivares,%20enviado) and
[Kevin Ruiz](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Kevin%20Ruiz) originally
appeared in the [September 15, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/09/15/politica/grito-de-
independencia-2026-miles-comienzan-a-llegar-al-zocalo-de-cdmx), Mexico’s
premier left-wing daily newspaper._

**Mexico City.** Just over 100,000 people have gathered on the esplanade of
the capital’s Zócalo ahead of the celebrations for the 216th anniversary of
the start of Mexico’s Independence, which will be led by President Claudia
Sheinbaum Pardo.

Since Tuesday afternoon, thousands of people began taking their places in
front of the National Palace, where **at 11:00 p.m. the President of the
Republic will appear on the central balcony to deliver the patriotic cheers.**
Some attendees are dressed in the national colors, with sombreros, sarapes,
and the now-traditional can of foam spray, used to douse others, whether
acquaintances or not. In addition, the mariachis of the Navy and National
Defense ministries take turns delighting those present with vernacular music.

![Revelers in front of the National Palace lit in
tricolor](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/grito-
body-1.jpg)Photo: Yazmín Ortega

Other attendees are already positioned in front of the stage, where the band
Intocable is expected to perform free of charge as part of the festivities. As
the night has progressed, the flow of people has increased in the Plaza de la
Constitución and its surrounding streets, awaiting the Cry of Independence
ceremony.

![](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/grito-de-
independencia-2026-miles-comienzan-a-llegar-al-zocalo-de-
cdmx_d2ee142b-7afb-413d-95db-e320f95c6f17_media-2-1024x768.webp)Photo: Yazmín
Ortega

For its part, the Secretariat of Citizen Security (SSC) deployed an operation
around the perimeter of the capital’s Zócalo, where officers check attendees
and remove prohibited objects.

**At 11:00 p.m., President Claudia Sheinbaum will appear on the central
balcony of the National Palace to lead the ceremony for the 216th anniversary
of the start of Mexico’s Independence.**
